predecessors.name: United States of Colombia
predecessors.text: the same territory, under the unitary and centralist constitution of 1886

ledger.x: 1886: Colombia becomes the Republic of Colombia, a centralised republic.
1928: the Tratado de Límites y Navegación Fluvial fixes the Apaporis-Amazon segment with Brazil; Cliopatria passes 3 cells (759 km2) near the Apaporis to Colombia.
1 September 1932: Peruvian civilians and soldiers seize Leticia.

wars.name: Thousand Days' War
wars.outcome: The page names it 'the most significant' of the civil wars; 'between 100 and 180 thousand Colombians lost their lives'.

wars.name: Colombia-Peru War
wars.outcome: The war 'lasted from September 1, 1932, to May 24, 1933'; the League of Nations commission took Leticia, and the League awarded the disputed area to Colombia in June 1934 (Rio de Janeiro Protocol, 1934).

certainty.note: The Amazon frontiers with Peru, Ecuador and Brazil are disputed until the 1922 treaty, the Brazilian treaties and the Leticia settlement; the Panama frontier is administrative until the secession of 1903.

The Peruvian frontier follows the 1922 treaty (ratified 1928) and the 1934 Rio Protocol, the Brazilian segment the 1928 treaty; the Venezuelan, Ecuadorian and Panamanian frontiers are not covered by the pages opened and stay as Cliopatria…
